subject: Duplicate AWS metering records across consolidated payer accounts — reconciliation & VAT reclassification
messages:
From: Julia Holt <julia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: eu-tax@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected duplicate charge lines in Dec settlements (Acme payer accounts)

Hi Ben —

We're reconciling December payouts and noticed two lines that look like duplicate metering records across our consolidated payer accounts. The net effect is a negative payout on the December settlement and our tax team is flagging VAT classification discrepancies because some usages were attributed to the EU entity and others to the UK payer. Attached is a short export from our side with the suspect SKUs and timestamps.

Can Redwood help determine whether these were double-reported by your integration with AWS Marketplace, or if these came from two different product listings that we should be consolidating? We need to sort this before our quarter close and confirm whether we'll be receiving any credit notes or invoice amendments.

Files attached: metering_report_Q4.xlsx

Thanks —
Julia Holt
Head of Finance, Acme Analytics
julia.holt@acme-analytics.com
+44 20 7000 1111

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Julia Holt <julia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charge lines in Dec settlements (Acme payer accounts)

Hi Julia — thanks for the heads up and for the export.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I will ask our billing ops team to pull the raw settlement logs and meter-to-listing mapping for December.
- Marissa, can you pull the AWS settlement export and the internal metering reconciliation for the Acme account(s)? Please include the payer IDs and listing IDs.
- We'll also open a case with AWS Marketplace to get the canonical settlement record if needed.

Two quick clarifying Qs for your tax team:
1) Which legal entity should receive the corrected invoice/credit? (Acme Analytics Ltd — UK, or Acme Analytics EU GmbH?)
2) If we issue credits, do you need us to provide VAT-detailed credit notes or just the settlement CSV?

If it's easier, happy to get on a 30m call later this week to align on the mutual action plan.

Ben
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Julia Holt <julia.holt@acme-analytics.com>, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Unexpected duplicate charge lines in Dec settlements — preliminary reconciliation

Ben / team — forwarding the initial reconciliation I ran. Summary:
- I matched the Acme metering export to our internal SKU mapping and AWS settlement logs.
- There are two listing IDs (prod-xyz and prod-xyz-legacy) that were both active in December and emitting the same usage meter for a subset of customers.
- Because the customer's organization had two linked payer IDs during the migration, the usage was recorded under both payer IDs for the same underlying meter event in AWS reporting. That caused double-counting in the settled lines and led to one negative adjustment when Marketplace applied a post-settlement correction.

Attached: aws-settlement-logs-2027-12.csv (trimmed), meter-to-listing_map_Q4.csv (internal), metering_report_Q4.xlsx (from Acme).

Action items I recommend:
1) Agree to issue credit notes for the double-billed amounts tied to the legacy listing (we can net against future payouts but better to issue explicit credits for tax audit trails).
2) Reclassify VAT on the affected invoice lines to the payer entity that actually consumed the service (Acme indicated UK entity for majority; Julia, please confirm).
3) Request AWS Marketplace to update the canonical settlement mapping and prevent duplicated meter propagation going forward (AWS support case opened).

I'll keep digging into the per-customer impacts; preliminary estimate is ~€18,400 gross exposure for December (will finalize by end of week).

—Marissa
Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Julia Holt <julia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 13:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Unexpected duplicate charge lines in Dec settlements — preliminary reconciliation

Thanks Marissa — this aligns with what the finance team was worried about. Laura / Legal: we should confirm the language on the credit note and VAT reversal so it satisfies an EU VAT audit. Specific asks for legal/tax review:
- Credit note must reference original invoice numbers and include VAT breakdown per line.
- We need to record the reason as "duplicate metering attribution due to legacy listing migration".
- Confirm whether Acme needs a VAT-detailed credit (yes/no) and which legal entity is receiving it.

Once Legal signs off, ops can draft the credit notes and I will approve. Ben / Marissa, coordinate timing with AWS case so we don't re-open the settlement after credit issuance.

Marcus
Head of Revenue — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Julia Holt <julia.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Duplicate AWS metering records — action plan and timeline

Julia — quick update and plan so we're all aligned:

What Redwood will do:
- Ops (Marissa) will prepare two VAT-detailed credit notes referencing the December invoices: one for amounts billed under the legacy listing and one for the corrected allocation.
- Legal (Laura) will review and approve the credit wording today.
- I'll coordinate sign-off with Marcus.
- We'll only issue the credits once AWS confirms the canonical settlement mapping (ticket MP-112233) so we avoid reversing/reposting twice.

Requested from Acme:
- Confirm which legal entity receives the credit: "Acme Analytics Ltd (UK)" or "Acme Analytics EU GmbH".
- Send VAT certificate for the receiving entity (VAT_cert_acme.pdf attached in your reply if available).

Target timeline: draft credit notes within 4 business days after legal OK; final issuance within 10 business days after AWS settlement confirmation.

If you want, let's do a 30m call Thursday to finalize entity and sign-off. Otherwise we'll proceed once we have the VAT cert and AWS confirmation.

Best,
Ben
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
